reasoning: This phase I dose-escalation trial failed at the first step of the causal chain. The study was designed to find the MTD of mithramycin in Ewing sarcoma patients, but encountered dose-limiting toxicity in 2/2 patients at the starting dose level (17.5 microgram/kg). This prevented dose escalation and achievement of potentially therapeutic exposures. While NR0B1 expression was measured as a biomarker for EWS-FLI1 pathway modulation, the severe toxicity at the lowest planned dose prevented adequate target engagement assessment. The 0% objective response rate in 6 evaluable patients and median time to progression of only 56 days suggest lack of efficacy, but this is secondary to the inability to reach tolerable therapeutic doses.

failure_modes.evidence: Dose limiting toxicity occurred in 2/2 patients at dose level 1 (17.5 microgram/kg), preventing dose escalation and MTD determination. Grade 3+ hepatotoxicity, hypotension, and fever were observed.
